name: What if my lot is too narrow for a detached in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: What if my lot is too narrow for a detached in-law suite?
mainEntity.text: What if my lot is too narrow for a detached in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: A narrow lot does not automatically rule out an in-law suite, but it usually changes the design strategy. Instead of forcing a detached unit that does not fit, homeowners often get better results from an attached addition, rear-facing conversion, or garage conversion. The key constraints are side-yard width, setbacks, fire access, drainage, and the ability to route plumbing and electrical service efficiently. Narrow lots also make it harder to preserve privacy, so the floor plan has to work harder. A feasibility study should test different layouts before anyone commits to one direction. The goal is to use the lot efficiently while avoiding a design that becomes expensive, cramped, or hard to approve.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the lot is too narrow for a detached suite, an attached addition, garage conversion, or interior conversion may still be possible. Narrow lots often limit setbacks, side-yard access, and fire separation, which makes compact designs more realistic. The right solution depends on available width, existing structures, and utility access.
